title: extcap: cache the results of --extcap-config
description:
Spawning a process to run --extcap-config can be expensive, particularly
on Windows. Cache the result of the command. Free the argument list when
freeing interfaces.

In some places where we internally want to retrieve the --extcap-config
results, pass back a const copy of the argument list stored in the hash
table so that we don't have to free it.

Bookmarks should have the same base --extcap-config as the parent extcap
interface but it's important to make sure that the device_name entry is
that of the bookmark, and that the preference pointers point to
preferences registered for the bookmark.

There might be extcaps where the --extcap-config response can be
dynamic. One common case is when underlying hardware interfaces change.
For some extcap users, the case where the config can be dynamic and the
case where the config can be especially long stem from the same
underlying cause - determining the extcap config requires some kind of
network or database query. I'm not really sure how to resolve both those
issues, which are in tension ("can change" argues for more queries;
takes long argues for less) other than to free the configuration when
the extcap interfaces are freed. That means that users might have to
select "Refresh Interfaces."

It might be nice to add a "Refresh this interface" option (context
menu?) for a particular extcap, though there's still some complications
there if it's a bookmark and the configuration is coming through the
parent interface.

Note in any case that dynamic configurations play havoc with stored
preferences.

This does not (yet) cache the entries for sub-options.

Fix #15779. Ping #15295
